answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to stake a costly, non-transferable resource before transacting — an onyx token minted only after verifiable work, so spinning up ten thousand fake agents costs ten thousand times the effort. Reputation then accrues slowly, like an ember nursed in a tundra campfire: new identities start with zero trust and earn it through repeated, checkable service, while any identity caught cheating forfeits its stake and history. Fakes stay cold and easy to spot; real agents warm up over time.
